text:
FPMC adds persistent user preference to a factorized directed transition: \(s(u,i)=p_u^Tq_i+a_{x_t}^Tb_i\), averaging the transition term over the previous basket when applicable. Separate source/target embeddings allow asymmetry; BPR learns rankings. Factorization shares evidence across transitions, but short user histories still poorly estimate user vectors, and first-order transitions omit broader context. [FPMC](https://archives.iw3c2.org/www2010/pub/pdfs/RendleFreudenthaler2010-FPMC.pdf). FOSSIL replaces the user vector with pooled historical item embeddings: \(s(u,i)=b_i+q_i^T[|H_u\setminus\{i\}|^{-\alpha}\sum_{j\in H_u\setminus\{i\}}p_j+\sum_{k=1}^K(\eta_k+\eta_{u,k})p_{x_{t-k+1}}]\). Shared item factors and only a few personalized lag weights improve sparse-user estimation; rare items and insufficient transition evidence remain limitations. [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152).

History-aggregating item-kNN variants score \(s(i)=\sum_k w_k\,\mathrm{sim}(x_{t-k+1},i)\), usually restricting contributions to stored neighbors. Recency weights emphasize current intent; older interactions supply broader preference evidence. This is a family, not one canonical equation: ordinary co-occurrence similarity need not encode direction, whereas sequential-rule counts explicitly encode earlier→later events, potentially across gaps. Last-item-only variants have no explicit long-term component. Count-based methods cannot generalize to unseen pairs; rare-pair estimates are noisy and popular targets dominate without normalization. [Definitions and comparisons](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.09587).

A proposed SASRec residual, \(s=s_{SASRec}+g(H)\sum_k w_k\widetilde T_{x_{t-k+1},i}\), therefore combines established ingredients. Here \(\widetilde T\) denotes popularity-adjusted directed counts. Unlike latent transitions, counts preserve specific observed edges but need smoothing, support shrinkage and calibrated scale; popularity correction can amplify rare-edge noise. Inference: inexpensive controls should include transition-only, recency-weighted item-kNN, SASRec plus a fixed-weight residual, and ablations removing direction, recency, popularity correction or gating. Compare validation macro HR@10 across all four categories; gains alone would not establish novelty of additive long-/short-term fusion.
